report:
### Conclusion
The claim that opening a bedroom window or door improves sleep quality is **supported by research evidence**. Opening windows or doors increases bedroom ventilation and prevents carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) accumulation, leading to better sleep quality and improved next-day cognitive function.

### Key Evidence
* **Reduced $\text{CO}_2$ Accumulation:** In unventilated bedrooms, overnight breathing causes $\text{CO}_2$ levels to rise. Studies show that opening windows or doors enhances ventilation, reduces indoor $\text{CO}_2$, and improves sleep quality (https://bizwhiznetwork.com/study-opening-windows-and-doors-improves-sleep-quality/, https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/windowdoor-opening-mediated-bedroom-ventilation-and-its-impact-on/).
* **Improved Sleep Metrics:** Controlled chamber studies demonstrate that lower indoor $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations minimize sleep disruptions caused by poor air freshness (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32979003/).
* **Next-Day Cognitive Performance:** Objective measurements reveal that lower bedroom $\text{CO}_2$ levels correlate with reduced morning sleepiness and superior next-day concentration and logical thinking ability (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/ina.12254).
